content.value_statement: Development teams can lose requirement evidence across planning, implementation, review, and release. This skill adds RVTF traceability while preserving Superpowers task boundaries and control.
actual_capabilities: Maps Superpowers workflow boundaries to RVTF requirements, acceptance items, journeys, and evidence.
Separates implementation checks, verification, formal review, and review-batch coverage.
Defines trace handling for plans, subagent tasks, code reviews, and branch completion.
Preserves host decisions while recording gaps, amendments, rulings, and residual risk.
Provides prompt additions for implementers, reviewers, and SDD controllers.
limitations: It does not replace Superpowers task grouping, review authority, or scheduling.
It does not execute commands, run tests, or inspect repositories automatically.
It requires the core tracing-requirements-to-verification skill and compatible host references.
Its mappings require re-audit when the pinned Superpowers revision changes.

use_cases.title: Plan Traceable Delivery
use_cases.description: Map plans and independently closable tasks to requirements, acceptance items, journeys, verification policy, and review coverage.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Subagent Work
use_cases.description: Add trace reporting to subagent-driven development without changing host task boundaries or creating unnecessary reviewers.

use_cases.title: Close Branches With Evidence
use_cases.description: Check item evidence, journey outcomes, review closure, gaps, amendments, and residual risk before branch completion.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this Superpowers plan to RVTF requirements, acceptance items, journeys, and verification evidence. Preserve the existing task boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Track an Implementation Task
prompt_templates.prompt: For each completed task, record the trace IDs advanced, evidence added, unresolved gaps, review findings, and scope amendments. Do not infer parent verification.

prompt_templates.title: Review Trace Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review every required acceptance item and applicable journey against target-specific evidence. Report missing mappings, path-order gaps, outcome gaps, and review limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Branch Completion
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform the final RVTF trace audit for this Superpowers branch. Check evidence validity, review closure, dispositions, amendments, required gaps, and residual-risk decisions before recommending completion.

output_examples.input: Map a plan with two implementation tasks and one verification task.
output_examples.output: The plan remains one Milestone. Each closable task becomes a Unit, while execution and verification groups remain separate. Each task receives trace mappings.
Completion requires consistent acceptance-item evidence, valid journey paths and outcomes, explicit dispositions for remaining objects, and a closed or controlled review epoch.

output_examples.input: A reviewer found an optional improvement after freeze.
output_examples.output: Keep the improvement deferred or rejected unless an authorized owner accepts a scope amendment. Do not restart an unrestricted review loop.

best_practices: Keep RVTF evidence separate from host execution status and review verdicts.
Record every scope amendment, ruling, gap, and continuation decision with trace impact.
Re-audit mappings when host workflows or pinned dependency revisions change.
anti_patterns: Do not treat task completion as proof of parent or journey verification.
Do not create reviewers solely because a review has multiple dimensions.
Do not use reusable evidence to bypass a required fresh host gate.

faq.question: Does this skill replace Superpowers?
faq.answer: No. It adds RVTF evidence and governance while Superpowers remains responsible for task grouping, roles, delegation, and host lifecycle decisions.

faq.question: What does RVTF add?
faq.answer: It connects requirements, acceptance items, journeys, evidence, gaps, reviews, and closure decisions across the host workflow.

faq.question: Does the skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and prompt additions. The host agent or user decides whether commands, tests, or reviews run.

faq.question: How should subagents report progress?
faq.answer: They should report advanced trace IDs, added evidence, gaps, review findings, and scope amendments without mutating copied item state.

faq.question: Can valid evidence skip a host gate?
faq.answer: Only when the gate freshness policy permits reuse. Reused evidence cannot erase a fresh host gate or support a current-test claim.

faq.question: When should this mapping be re-audited?
faq.answer: Re-audit it before use when Superpowers behavior, the required tracing skill, or the pinned host revision changes.
